titulo: Exploring Fashion and Expressing Opinions Through Time
titulo_es: La moda a través del tiempo y la expresión de opiniones
estandares: Describo procesos que empezaron en el pasado y continúan. Expreso, sustento y contrasto opiniones sobre gustos, estilos y cambios sociales.
competencias: Usar el presente perfecto continuo para procesos en curso; emplear modales para expresar posibilidad y deducción; hablar de horas, fechas y siglos; describir ropa y accesorios; argumentar y responder a opiniones ajenas.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: En grupos, los estudiantes eligen una década (los 60, 80, 2000) y presentan cómo vestía la gente, qué ha cambiado desde entonces y sustentan con argumentos por qué ese estilo vuelve o no.
proyecto.descripcion_en: In groups, students choose a decade (the 60s, 80s, 2000s) and present how people dressed, what has changed since then, and argue why that style is or is not coming back.

lecciones.content_es:
Cómo se forma

have / has been + verbo-ing: I have been studying for two hours.

Para qué sirve

  • Una acción que empezó antes y sigue ocurriendo: She has been working here since March.
  • Una acción reciente cuyo efecto se ve: You look tired. Have you been running?
  • Enfatizar la duración, no el resultado: They've been waiting for an hour.

Con for y since

for + duración (for two hours, for a long time) · since + punto de inicio (since 2020, since Monday).

Ojo

Los verbos de estado (know, be, have de posesión) no usan esta forma: se dice I have known her for years, no I have been knowing.
lecciones.content_en:
How it is formed

have / has been + verb-ing: I have been studying for two hours.

What it is for

  • An action that started before and is still going on: She has been working here since March.
  • A recent action whose effect is visible: You look tired. Have you been running?
  • Emphasizing duration, not the result: They've been waiting for an hour.

With for and since

for + duration (for two hours) · since + starting point (since 2020).

Careful

State verbs (know, be, have meaning possession) do not use this form: say I have known her for years, not I have been knowing.

lecciones.content_es:
Resultado o proceso

  • Simple → el resultado, lo terminado: I've written three emails. (están hechos)
  • Continuo → el proceso, la duración: I've been writing emails all morning. (quizá sigo)

Con cantidad, siempre simple

Si dices cuántos, va el simple: She has read five books this month, no has been reading five books.

Con duración, casi siempre continuo

She has been reading all afternoon.

Con live, work y study

Con estos tres verbos y for/since los dos son válidos y significan casi lo mismo: I've lived here for ten years = I've been living here for ten years.
lecciones.content_en:
Result or process

  • Simple → the result, what is finished: I've written three emails.
  • Continuous → the process, the duration: I've been writing emails all morning.

With a quantity, always simple

If you say how many, use the simple: She has read five books this month, not has been reading five books.

With a duration, usually continuous

She has been reading all afternoon.

With live, work and study

With these three verbs and for/since both forms are valid and mean almost the same: I've lived here for ten years = I've been living here for ten years.

lecciones.content_es:
Qué tan seguro estás

  • must – casi seguro que sí: She must be at home; the light is on.
  • may / might / could – es posible: It might rain later.
  • can't – casi seguro que no: He can't be 40; he looks much younger.

Ojo con la negación

La deducción negativa es can't, no mustn't. mustn't significa prohibido, no «seguro que no».

Otros usos

  • Consejo: should / ought to — You should try that jacket.
  • Permiso formal: may — May I try it on?
  • Petición educada: could / would — Could you show me another size?

Todos van con el verbo en base y no llevan -s ni to.
lecciones.content_en:
How sure you are

  • must – almost certainly yes: She must be at home; the light is on.
  • may / might / could – it is possible: It might rain later.
  • can't – almost certainly not: He can't be 40; he looks much younger.

Careful with the negative

The negative deduction is can't, not mustn't. mustn't means forbidden, not "surely not".

Other uses

  • Advice: should / ought to — You should try that jacket.
  • Formal permission: may — May I try it on?
  • Polite request: could / would — Could you show me another size?

They all take the base verb and never add -s or to.

lecciones.content_es:
La hora

Formal: It's a quarter past nine. It's twenty to six.
Digital: It's nine fifteen. It's five forty.
a.m. antes del mediodía, p.m. después. Noon es mediodía y midnight medianoche.

Fechas

on August 7th, 1819 → on August the seventh, eighteen nineteen.

Años

  • 1985 → nineteen eighty-five
  • 1900 → nineteen hundred
  • 2008 → two thousand eight
  • 2026 → twenty twenty-six

Siglos y décadas

the 20th century = del año 1901 al 2000. the 1980s (se lee the nineteen eighties) son «los ochenta».

The time

Formal: It's a quarter past nine. It's twenty to six.
Digital: It's nine fifteen. It's five forty.
a.m. before noon, p.m. after. Noon is 12:00 and midnight is 00:00.

Dates

on August 7th, 1819 → on August the seventh, eighteen nineteen.

Years

  • 1985 → nineteen eighty-five
  • 1900 → nineteen hundred
  • 2008 → two thousand eight
  • 2026 → twenty twenty-six

Centuries and decades

the 20th century covers 1901 to 2000. the 1980s (read the nineteen eighties) means the eighties.

Prepositions: in the 90s, in the 19th century, on July 4th, at 8 p.m.

Prendas

hoodie (buzo con capucha), blouse, suit (traje), tie (corbata), vest (chaleco), leggings, overalls (overol), sneakers (tenis), sandals, heels (tacones), raincoat.

Accesorios

belt (cinturón), watch, earrings (aretes), necklace (collar), bracelet, ring, sunglasses, backpack, purse / handbag.

Describir un atuendo

Orden: opinión → tamaño → edad → color → material.
a beautiful long black leather jacket.

Materiales y estilos

cotton (algodón), wool (lana), leather (cuero), denim (mezclilla), silk (seda). Estilos: casual, formal, sporty, vintage, trendy (a la moda), outfit (conjunto).

lecciones.t: Hablar de la moda a través del tiempo
lecciones.content_es:
Used to: lo que antes era y ya no

used to + verbo base describe hábitos o estados pasados que ya terminaron: People used to wear hats every day.

  • Negativo: They didn't use to wear jeans. (sin -d)
  • Pregunta: Did people use to dress like that?

Verbos de cambio

become (volverse), turn into, go out of fashion (pasar de moda), come back (volver), catch on (ponerse de moda), disappear.

Expresiones de época

back then, in those days, nowadays, these days, ever since, over the years.

Back then everyone wore bell-bottoms; nowadays they're coming back.
lecciones.content_en:
Used to: what was true and is not anymore

used to + base verb describes past habits or states that are over: People used to wear hats every day.

  • Negative: They didn't use to wear jeans. (no -d)
  • Question: Did people use to dress like that?

Verbs of change

become, turn into, go out of fashion, come back, catch on, disappear.

Time expressions

back then, in those days, nowadays, these days, ever since, over the years.

Back then everyone wore bell-bottoms; nowadays they're coming back.

lecciones.t_en: Arguing and supporting points of view
lecciones.content_es:
Dar tu opinión

I think… · I believe… · In my opinion… · From my point of view… · As far as I'm concerned… · If you ask me…

Estar de acuerdo

I agree. · Exactly! · I couldn't agree more. · That's true. · You have a point there.

Estar en desacuerdo

I disagree. · I'm sorry, but I can't agree with that. · I see your point, but… · Perhaps, but… · I'm not so sure about that.

Sustentar

because, since, as (razón) · for example, for instance, such as (ejemplo) · therefore, that's why, as a result (consecuencia) · on the other hand (por otro lado).

Ojo con la cortesía

Un desacuerdo directo (You're wrong) suena agresivo en inglés. Se suaviza: I see your point, but I think…
lecciones.content_en:
Giving your opinion

I think… · I believe… · In my opinion… · From my point of view… · As far as I'm concerned… · If you ask me…

Agreeing

I agree. · Exactly! · I couldn't agree more. · That's true. · You have a point there.

Disagreeing

I disagree. · I'm sorry, but I can't agree with that. · I see your point, but… · Perhaps, but… · I'm not so sure about that.

Supporting

because, since, as (reason) · for example, for instance, such as (example) · therefore, that's why, as a result (consequence) · on the other hand.

Careful with politeness

A blunt disagreement (You're wrong) sounds aggressive in English. Soften it: I see your point, but I think…

fichas.d: Reconoce que el otro tiene razón en algo.
fichas.d_en: Acknowledges the other person is partly right.

fichas.d_en: A softened, polite disagreement.

repaso.titulo: Repaso — Exploring Fashion and Expressing Opinions
repaso.titulo_en: Review — Exploring Fashion and Expressing Opinions
repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Dos herramientas se combinan: el presente perfecto continuo para procesos que vienen ocurriendo, y los modales para decir qué tan seguro estás de algo. Con eso se describe cómo ha cambiado la moda y se sustenta una opinión.

Puntos gramaticales

  • have been + -ing enfatiza duración; el perfecto simple enfatiza resultado.
  • Con cantidad exacta siempre va el simple.
  • must = casi seguro que sí; can't = casi seguro que no; might/may/could = posible.
  • used to + verbo base para hábitos pasados; en negativo, use to.

Vocabulario

Horas, fechas, años y siglos; ropa, accesorios y orden de adjetivos; verbos de cambio; fórmulas para opinar, acordar y discrepar con cortesía.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

Two tools combine: the present perfect continuous for ongoing processes, and modals for how sure you are about something. With those you describe how fashion has changed and support an opinion.

Grammar points

  • have been + -ing emphasizes duration; the perfect simple emphasizes result.
  • With an exact quantity always use the simple.
  • must = almost certainly yes; can't = almost certainly not; might/may/could = possible.
  • used to + base verb for past habits; in the negative, use to.

Vocabulary

Hours, dates, years and centuries; clothes, accessories and adjective order; verbs of change; formulas to give opinions, agree and disagree politely.
